items.title: Lead Data Engineer
items.description: About Better Collective Sports media at scale, running on data Better Collective is a global sports media group, reaching more than 400 million monthly visits across a portfolio of leading sports media brands. We build products and experiences that make sports more engaging and accessible for fans around the world. Behind that sits a large and diverse technology and data landscape, spanning markets, brands and business models. We work in a collaborative environment where people are encouraged to challenge how things are done, take ownership and help shape what comes next. The domain Paid media is where the data has to pay off. We spend real money across dozens of ad networks every day. Which campaigns scale, which creatives get cut, which markets get more budget: those calls come out of the models this team builds. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue, CRM data, all stitched into one user-level view of what a click was actually worth. That model exists and it works. It is also the most demanding domain on our data platform - the most sources, the fastest schema churn, and the shortest patience for a table that landed late. We are looking for the engineer who owns it. Where this role sits A central platform team sets the how. You set the what. Better Collective runs a hub and spoke data organisation. A central data platform team owns the platform itself - MotherDuck, dbt, Dagster, DLT, the golden paths, the standards, the infrastructure. Paid Media Insights is a domain team, a spoke, that builds on it. The split is deliberate and we hold to it. The platform team decides how data is produced here. You decide what paid media produces, and you own everything we run. So you are not starting a new stack, and you are not going to spend your year on plumbing that a central team should be solving once for everyone. You are, however, expected to be a demanding customer. When a golden path does not fit paid media, we want you to say so and push for it to change, not quietly build around it. You will report to the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights and work across Paid Media, with the Campaign, Commercial and CRM teams, as well as with the central platform team. What you will own Every data job in paid media. All of it. Freshness, cost, reliability, alerting, and the incident at 07:30 before the spend review. If a paid media model is wrong or late, it is yours, not the platform team's. That accountability is the core of this role, not a footnote to it. Concretely, you will own: The end-to-end user-level model. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue, and CRM, joined into one view the business trusts enough to move budget on. Ingestion of paid media sources, built on the platform's framework. Which sources, which schemas, and what happens the next time a network changes its API without telling anyone. The domain's models, from staging through to the marts analysts and business teams actually query, plus the semantic meaning that sits on top of them. Nobody at the centre can define what a qualified signup means in paid media. You can. Reverse ETL back into the ad platforms, so online and offline conversion data lands where it changes bidding. The handover. Part of your first year is taking over the paid media jobs the central team still runs on our behalf, and moving that ownership to where the context actually lives. What you will lead A group of engineers, and the standard they build to You will guide and mentor a group of data engineers in Paid Media Insights, as their technical lead. That means setting the standard for how this domain builds, reviewing their work, unblocking them, and deliberately growing them: giving away the interesting problems rather than keeping them. You will also shape the domain's roadmap together with the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, the analysts and the business teams, and you will represent paid media in platform conversations, including how we support machine learning and data science on top of this data. This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not a step away from building. You will be in the code. What we are looking for More than a stack match, we are looking for a particular way of working. You take ownership, and it shows up in the boring parts. Plenty of engineers want to design the model. You also want the pager. You would rather own a domain end to end, unglamorous parts included, than build one piece and hand off the consequences. When things get tricky, you follow through. You break complex systems into simple parts. Paid media data is genuinely messy: attribution windows, late conversions, identity across platforms, and dozens of source APIs that all disagree. You can hold that complexity and still hand the business something they can reason about. You raise the people around you. You are the person colleagues come to for technical advice, and you enjoy that part of the job. You give feedback that lands, you review generously, and you would rather the whole team understand the pipeline than be the only one who does. You work well with a platform team. You have strong opinions about standards and you are still happy to work inside someone else's. You know the difference between a constraint worth fighting and a preference worth dropping, and you would rather help fix a shared path than fork it. You are already past prompting. AI is part of how you engineer, not something you occasionally ask questions. You have experimented with agents, tooling or AI-enabled workflows, and you have a view on what a data domain has to look like for them to be useful on top of it: documented, standardised, semantically clear. Paid media is likely where we find out first. You are close to the business. You will sit with marketers and analysts who are spending budget on what you build. You want that proximity, and you can talk about data with people who do not think in tables. You are technically deep where it counts. Production pipelines in SQL and Python, modelling and orchestration tooling such as dbt and Dagster, cloud data warehousing, and a real feel for performance, cost and reliability at scale. Experience with paid media or attribution data, or with machine learning pipelines, is a bonus rather than a requirement. Not sure you meet every single requirement? That is okay. Your unique experience might be exactly what we are looking for. Our stack What you will build on MotherDuck / DuckDB · dbt · Dagster · DLT · Python · SQL · AWS · reverse ETL and semantic layer tooling We do not expect you to have worked with all of these. If you have built production pipelines on Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift and you are curious about where we are going, that transfers. What we offer An international company in growth, and a flat structure Join a strong team where you can create value and make a real business impact, in a dynamic and creative environment with a flat organisational structure. Freedom with responsibility, ample room to grow, and the chance to take on a broad set of responsibilities. Flexible working hours supporting a healthy work-life balance, private health insurance, and office perks including lunch, snacks, gym access and social events, alongside skilled, passionate and fun colleagues. Your path to Better Collective How to apply We process applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions about the position, reach out to Michael Hill, Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, at mhill@bettercollective.com. We look forward to hearing from you.

As a software engineer on this team, you will build the identity, vetting, and access management infrastructure that underpins our trusted access programs, along with the monitoring and enforcement tooling that keeps them safe. go-to-market teams so that access decisions are well-informed and consistently applied Build systems that identify account compromise and takeover, apply mitigations in real time, and carry affected accounts through to full remediation Design and build the dashboards, alerting, and internal admin tooling that give the team and its partners clear visibility into the health and outcomes of our access programs Integrate with third-party identity verification and data enrichment vendors You may be a good fit if you have: A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or comparable experience Experience building and operating backend systems in production Strong coding skills in at least one general-purpose programming language, and experience building software with AI coding tools Strong communication skills and ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders Care about the societal impacts of AI and want your work to make powerful items.description: About the Team The Applied AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. About the Role As an Applied AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business”, shaping each customer's AI strategy and guiding their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact. You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate business priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value and growth. The Account Director owns commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value. You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong industry fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. About The Job As a member of the Partner Solution Architecture Team, you will work closely with our Partner and GTM teams to drive the adoption of our state-of-the-art enterprise AI platform and models. What you will do - Help onboard Mistral solutions and models to strategic ISV and Tech partner platforms - Execute on effective technical discovery with partners to understand potential clients' needs, challenges, and desired outcomes in collaboration with GTM - Drive enablement at scale across strategic partner technical and sales teams - Create and update assets for partner enablement: technical demos, enablement videos, reference architectures, etc. - Support partners in identifying, qualifying, and disqualifying opportunities where Mistral solutions can unlock the most value for the customer - Represent Mistral AI at partner, customer, and industry events, including executive briefings, conferences, and developer gatherings - Collaborate with Mistral teams, from Science, Product, Engineering, Support, and GTM to progress and support deals, as well as providing expertise and insights where necessary What we look for - Experience in a technical partner presales, solutions architect, or consulting role with heavy partner and customer-facing exposure. - A track record of building enablement assets and driving evangelism at scale across partner organizations - Experience partnering with ISVs or Technology Partners, driving technical account strategy, proof-of-concept scoping and support, and execution - Strong Python or TypeScript skills - Working knowledge of cloud architecture and deployment patterns for AI and ML solutions - Familiarity with MEDDPICC and Command of the Message. - Working knowledge of Generative AI serving architectures, e.g. vLLM - Working knowledge of Kubernetes WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page https://www.kraken.com/culture to understand what drives us and how we work. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. CE Social delivers exceptional customer support and community engagement for Kraken across social media. We answer questions, resolve concerns, and drive conversations in our communities, never shying away from engaging with clients and prospects alike. We're fast, resourceful, and proud to represent Kraken's voice publicly. We're Kraken's eyes and ears on social, and our goal is to run the best social support team in the financial space. As part of CE Social, you'll monitor and engage with clients on social media as a first point of contact for support, handling real-time conversations, account-related questions, and troubleshooting with Kraken's six-star standard of care. You'll be responsible for supporting all of Payward's brands on social, replying to inquiries across our Kraken, Kraken Pro, Krak, Payward, xStocks, Breakout Prop, and NinjaTrader handles. You'll also partner with internal teams to resolve complex issues and contribute to projects that improve the client experience. You're a voice for Kraken in public, helping build its reputation for great client care and community engagement. THE OPPORTUNITY - Monitor social channels and respond promptly to client inquiries - Work across multiple social platforms at once, prioritizing by urgency and volume - Moderate our social communities and enforce community guidelines - Proactively engage clients to grow Kraken's voice and presence on social - Partner with internal teams on complex cases and process improvements - Participate in team meetings, projects, and training sessions - Stay current on new crypto trends, products, and technologies, and on Kraken's own product suite WHAT YOU BRING - 3+ years of experience in social media management, community management, or customer support - Genuine crypto OG experience and knowledge, with a strong pulse on the APAC crypto scene and familiarity with Chinese crypto culture on social media. You're plugged into the space, know the key players, and stay on top of what's happening. - Hands-on, user-side experience across platforms like X, Reddit, Telegram, LinkedIn, Discord, Facebook, and Instagram, plus app store reviews and Trustpilot. Crypto-native experience strongly preferred. - Familiar with Sprinklr and social media management platforms, as well as tools like Zendesk, Jira/Confluence, and Slack. - Sharp attention to detail and the judgment to read intent and tone in client messages - Resilience and multitasking ability for high-volume, high-pressure queues - Comfortable knowing your work is public-facing as every reply is visible - Flexibility to work scheduled shifts (between 4 am to 12 pm UTC), including weekends - Fluent in English and Chinese Mandarin, with confidence writing in Simplified Chinese. Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. About the Role We’re looking for a Rack Power Engineer with deep expertise in high-power conversion and distribution to design, qualify, and support power systems for AI supercomputers. You will own rack power solutions—including power shelves, AC/DC rectifiers, power supply units (PSUs), power management controllers (PMCs), and high-current distribution—from requirements and supplier development through deployment. You will also monitor fleet rack power health, lead debugging and root-cause investigations, and drive improvements into hardware, firmware, and qualification coverage. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Own rack power architecture and requirements for high-power AI supercomputing systems, including power budgets, AC input interfaces, DC distribution, redundancy, efficiency, serviceability, and integration with data center infrastructure. - Drive the design and supplier development of power shelves, rectifiers, PSUs, PMCs, busbars, connectors, and protection circuits. Review electrical designs and control behavior, and evaluate performance, cost, reliability, and availability trade-offs. - Define and execute component, shelf, and rack qualification plans covering load transients, current sharing, hot-swap, startup and shutdown, redundancy failover, fault protection and recovery, thermal limits, and AC disturbances and ride-through. - Partner with firmware and software teams to define and validate PMC functionality, telemetry, alarms, power sequencing, power capping, and fault handling. Verify communication interfaces, firmware updates, interoperability, and regression coverage. - Characterize rack power under representative AI workloads. Drive supplier test reviews, manufacturing test coverage, and closure of power-related issues. - Evaluate emerging rack power technologies, including higher-voltage DC distribution and battery or supercapacitor energy storage.
